abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>In wheat, strong genetic correlations have been found between grain yield (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GY</jats:styled-content>) and tiller number per plant (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TN</jats:styled-content>), fertile spikelet number per spike (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">FSN</jats:styled-content>), kernel number per spike (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">KN</jats:styled-content>) and thousand‐kernel weight (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TKW</jats:styled-content>). To investigate their genetic relationships at the individual quantitative trait locus (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content>) level, we performed both normal and multivariate conditional <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> analysis based on two recombinant inbred lines (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">RIL</jats:styled-content>s) populations. A total of 79 and 48 normal <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content>s were identified in the International Triticeae Mapping Initiative (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ITMI</jats:styled-content>)/<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SHW</jats:styled-content>‐L1 × Chuanmai 32 (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SC</jats:styled-content>) populations, respectively, as well as 55 and 35 conditional <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content>s. Thirty‐two <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> clusters in the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ITMI</jats:styled-content> population and 18 <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> clusters in the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SC</jats:styled-content> population explained 0.9%–46.2% of phenotypic variance for two to eight traits. A comparison between the normal and conditional <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> mapping analyses indicated that <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">FSN</jats:styled-content> made the smallest contribution to <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GY</jats:styled-content> among the four <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GY</jats:styled-content> components that were considered at the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> level. The effects of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TN</jats:styled-content>,<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case"> KN</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TKW</jats:styled-content> on <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GY</jats:styled-content> were stronger at the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> level.</jats:p>
title: Analysis of contributors to grain yield in wheat at the individual quantitative trait locus level
